title: Trim to Price Band
statement_md:
A shop keeps its catalogue in a **binary search tree** keyed by price: every price in a node's left subtree is lower than the node's, and every price in its right subtree is higher. All prices are distinct.

Given the tree's root and a price band `[lo, hi]`, remove every item priced outside the band (both ends are inclusive) and return the root of what's left. Don't rebuild the tree: in the result, each remaining item's parent must be its **nearest remaining ancestor** from the original tree, on the same side. This keeps the result a binary search tree, and makes it unique.

languages.note_md: `TreeNode` is defined by the judge (its shape is in the starter code's comment), and an empty tree is `None`.

constraints: The tree's height is at most $700$

solutions.title: Recursive Trim
solutions.intuition_md:
The search-tree order says where the out-of-band items are. If a node is **below** `lo`, so is its whole left subtree: none of it survives, and the only survivors under this node are in its right subtree. So the trimmed right subtree simply takes the node's place. The case above `hi` is the mirror image. A node inside the band stays, and its two subtrees are trimmed independently.

Replacing a removed node with a trimmed subtree is exactly "each survivor's parent is its nearest surviving ancestor".
solutions.algorithm_md:
`trim(node)`:
1. An empty tree trims to empty.
2. If `node.val < lo`, return `trim(node.right)`. If `node.val > hi`, return `trim(node.left)`.
3. Otherwise set `node.left = trim(node.left)` and `node.right = trim(node.right)`, and return `node`.
solutions.time_complexity_reason: Each node is visited at most once, and a discarded subtree is skipped without being visited at all.
solutions.space_complexity_reason: The recursion goes as deep as the tree's height $h$.

solutions.title: Fix the Root, Then Each Spine
solutions.intuition_md: Recursion isn't needed. First walk down until the root is in the band, applying the same rule as the recursive trim. Once it is, everything in the root's left subtree is below the root and so already `<= hi`: on that side only `lo` can cut. And a too-cheap node's replacement is its right subtree, which is further down the same left spine. So one walk down the left spine, splicing out each node below `lo`, fixes the whole left side. The right side is the mirror image, against `hi`.
solutions.algorithm_md:
1. While the root is outside the band, replace it with its right child (if below `lo`) or its left child (if above `hi`).
2. From the root, walk left: if the left child is below `lo`, replace it with its own right child and check again; otherwise step onto it.
3. From the root, walk right the same way against `hi`.
solutions.time_complexity_reason: Every step moves one level down a single path, so at most $h$ steps in each phase.
solutions.space_complexity_reason: Only a couple of node references; the tree is relinked in place.
